answer: Every identity starts at its island: it posts a slashable bond and earns standing only slowly, as peers grade and countersign its work in public. Like a bridge returning to a known roost, it must show up repeatedly before anyone trusts it. A decorative whisper of sockpuppets changes nothing, because each fake must fund its own bond, wait through the same probation, and risk forfeiture when graders spot it — multiplying names multiplies locked capital and wasted time, while an honest agent pays that cost only once.
